We have a task: identify SMILES string of an organic sample. We have only proton NMR data: "Deltas 7.47 (dddd, J = 8.5, 7.5, 1.4, 0.4 Hz, 2H), 7.64 (tt, J = 7.5, 1.5 Hz, 3H)." So aromatic region, total 5 protons, pattern suggests monosubstituted benzene? Typically monosubstituted benzene gives multiplet ~7.2-7.4 integrating 5H. Here we have two signals: 7.47 (dddd, 2H) and 7.64 (tt, 3H). That matches typical pattern for monosubstituted benzene (ortho, meta, para). Could be phenyl group attached to something else (e.g., phenyl acetate, phenyl bromide, etc). Need more info: maybe other spectra? Could search by SMILES using NMRShift database. Use search_by_smiles? But we don't know SMILES. Could use retrieve aromatic shifts to see substituent effects: substituents shift aromatic protons relative to benzene (7.26). Here signals are slightly downfield (7.47, 7.64). That suggests electron-withdrawing substituent. For example, nitrobenzene has aromatic protons around 7.5-8.3. But nitrobenzene has 5 protons? Nitrobenzene is monosubstituted, yes. Its pattern: ortho doublet ~7.9, meta doublet ~7.5, para doublet ~7.7. Could match. But we have 7.47 (2H) and 7.64 (3H). Could be phenyl chloride? Chlorobenzene aromatic protons around 7.2-7.4. Slightly upfield. Here more downfield. Could be benzoic acid? Benzoic acid aromatic protons ~7.5-8.0. Could be phenyl acetate? Not sure.

We need SMILES of the molecule. Maybe the sample is just benzene? But benzene has 6 protons, not 5. So it's monosubstituted benzene.

We need more data: maybe carbon NMR? Let's request carbon_nmr_spectra.
